input: Set a hard stop time for work each evening

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing what counts as 'work' determines what must stop — emails, Slack, deep work, or all screens — which shapes the boundary being set.
The target stop time itself is the central constraint; without it, no alarm, block, or ritual can be scheduled.
Whether the user works from home, an office, or hybrid changes which enforcement mechanisms are practical (e.g., leaving the building vs. app blockers).
If a manager, team, or clients regularly contact them after hours, accountability and boundary-setting involve other people and need a different approach.
The tools or systems the user already uses (phone alarms, calendar blocks, app blockers, a shutdown ritual) determine the most actionable next step.
Defining what 'sticking to it' looks like — e.g., 5 out of 7 nights, zero exceptions, or allowed flexibility — sets a measurable bar and avoids all-or-nothing thinking.
Whether the user wants a gradual wind-down routine vs. an abrupt stop, and what they want to transition into, shapes how the boundary is designed and made sustainable.

gold.taskTitle: Set a hard stop time for work each evening
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to establish and consistently honour a fixed cut-off time that ends their workday every evening.

questions.title: What specific time do you want to stop working?
questions.description: Identify the exact target hard stop time the user wants to enforce each evening.

questions.title: What counts as 'work' that must stop at that time?
questions.description: Clarify whether the boundary applies to all work activity (email, Slack, deep work, calls) or only certain types.

questions.title: Do you work from home, an office, or both?
questions.description: Understand the physical work context to determine which enforcement strategies are realistic.

questions.title: Do colleagues, clients, or a manager message you after hours?
questions.description: Determine whether other people are a factor in boundary-breaking, which may require communication or notification strategies.

questions.title: What tools or devices do you use most for work?
questions.description: Identify the platforms and devices in play so the right blockers, alarms, or automations can be recommended.

questions.title: How consistently do you need to hit this limit to feel successful?
questions.description: Define the user's standard for success — strict every night, a weekly average, or flexibility on certain days.

questions.title: Do you want a wind-down transition or a clean abrupt stop?
questions.description: Understand whether the user prefers a gradual shutdown ritual leading up to the stop time or a hard, immediate cut-off.
